shouldFix.title: The carrier-domain repair leaves one predicate unregistered and supplies no usable closed value shape for policy provenance
evidence: policyProvenance now has two consentCarrier-discriminated predicates: nullWhen invocation-time-naming and requiredWhen pre-existing-policy. consentCarrierPredicateDomain.appliesTo enumerates only the nullWhen path, and the member supplies nullWhenDomain but no requiredWhenDomain.

The same member adds closedValuesWhenPresent as boolean true. Everywhere else in this contract and every recorded host-effect predecessor that uses this key, its value is an array containing the actual legal strings. No policy-provenance value list or closed source-identity shape is supplied here.

FC-CARRIER-SHAPE proves the presence/null branch matrix with descriptive placeholders, but it supplies no concrete lawful policy source identity and therefore cannot resolve the malformed value constraint.
shouldFix.impact: The prose makes the intended two carrier branches understandable, so this is not a blocker. The machine-facing declaration is nevertheless internally incomplete: a structural checker following appliesTo misses requiredWhen, while a checker following the established closedValuesWhenPresent shape receives a boolean instead of a value domain. Implementations can therefore disagree on how to validate the pre-existing-policy branch.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Register both policyProvenance.nullWhen and policyProvenance.requiredWhen under consentCarrierPredicateDomain (or give each an explicit domain). Replace closedValuesWhenPresent: true with an actual finite value list if the provenance vocabulary is closed, or with an explicit non-empty/bounded source-identity type or closed object shape if it is not. Exercise that typed value in FC-CARRIER-SHAPE.
